claim: `tprod_nonneg` unnecessarily assumes `[L.NeBot]`; the conclusion `0 ≤ ∏'[L] x, f x` still holds when `¬ L.NeBot` (where `tprod` reduces to a `finprod`).
requested_change:
Drop the `[L.NeBot]` assumption and handle the `¬ L.NeBot` case by rewriting with `tprod_bot`, then splitting on `f.mulSupport.Finite` and using `finprod_eq_prod` + `Finset.prod_nonneg` (finite case) or `finprod_of_infinite_mulSupport` (infinite case). One possible proof (verified with `lean_verify_edit`) is:
```lean
by
  classical
  by_cases hL : L.NeBot
  · by_cases h : Multipliable f L
    · exact ge_of_tendsto' h.hasProd fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ hf i
    · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
  · by_cases hfin : f.mulSupport.Finite
    · simpa [tprod_bot hL, finprod_eq_prod _ hfin] using
        (hfin.toFinset.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ hf i)
    · simp [tprod_bot hL, finprod_of_infinite_mulSupport hfin]
```
